paragraphs: Friend, this passage is the last stop in the fall of Judah, and it is a rough ride. A governor is put in place, he promises the commanders that "it will be well with you," and then he is struck down at Mizpah (2 Kings 25:24-25). The people and the commanders run to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans (2 Kings 25:26). Plans fall apart in this chapter, and the people holding them fall apart too, and I think that part is heavy.

Then the story turns to Babylon, and a king who has sat in prison for thirty-seven years (2 Kings 25:27). Evil-merodach "released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison" and "spoke kindly to Jehoiachin" (2 Kings 25:27-28). Jehoiachin changes out of his prison clothes and eats at the king's table "for the rest of his life" (2 Kings 25:29). The book of Kings ends with a king of David's line out of prison and fed, not with a throne rebuilt or a trip home. I know a little about being pulled out of the dark, and I never saw it coming either.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. When everything around you is falling apart, the story is not over, and a small kindness is a real kindness. The text doesn't say why it happened, so I won't guess, but I do know the door to that prison opened. Keep your ovens warm, friend, because you never know when your door is going to swing open.
